component: HOME phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001): up to 3 dwelling units per lot, including tiny homes
coverage: Citywide, lots zoned SF-1, SF-2 and SF-3
coding_notes: effective_date is the date the city began accepting applications (2024-02-05); the city page gives no separate effective date. Also removes the primary/secondary distinction and the accessory-apartment and guest-house use categories (ADUs become 2- and 3-unit uses), and the limit on unrelated adults. Two- and three-unit uses: 40% building coverage, 45% impervious cover. FAR tiers by unit count not coded (the ordinance text was not read; not on the city summary page). Single-family use stays under Subchapter F (McMansion). Parking: see TX-4805000-parking-2023. Second coder (2026-10-18): applications-open date confirmed as the start date. Ben noted the city's current guidance that lots created before 2025-06-16 with no more than four units need no drainage review, which suggests a later change allowing a fourth unit; phase 1 itself is coded at 3. A later change needs its own row with a source (open).

component: HOME phase 2 (Ord. 20240516-006): small-lot single-family, one unit on lots of at least 1,800 sq ft (was 5,750)
coverage: SF-1, SF-2, SF-3 lots outside the Wildland-Urban Interface and Uprooted Report areas
coding_notes: effective_date is when applications were first accepted. Lots 1,800 to <5,750 sq ft; impervious cover follows base zoning; not eligible for the Preservation Bonus. lot_split=True reads the smaller minimum as allowing subdivision into small lots.

component: HOME phase 2 extended to the remaining areas (citywide)
coverage: SF-1, SF-2, SF-3 lots citywide, adding Wildland-Urban Interface and Uprooted Report areas
coding_notes: Same rules as phase 2a; only coverage widens on 2024-11-16 (city page: applications accepted citywide).

component: Citywide elimination of minimum off-street parking requirements
parking: no minimum; accessible parking still required
coverage: Citywide, all uses, except Hyde Park, North Hyde Park, North University and Fairview Park, which keep their existing minimums for now
coding_notes: Council vote 8-2 on 2023-11-02. Effective date not found in the sources opened: coded as the vote date (needs the ordinance text). Confounder for HOME phase 1 (same window).

component: Chapter 42 amendment: by-right minimum single-family lot cut from 5,000 to 3,500 sq ft in the urban area; lots down to 1,400 sq ft with compensating open space or performance standards
coding_notes: Adopted 1998, took effect 1999 (Regulatory Review); exact day not found, effective_date coded as 1999-01-01 (year precision only). Houston has no zoning: these are subdivision (Chapter 42) rules; deed restrictions can still forbid small lots. Mercatus: lots averaging 1,400 sq ft need 600 sq ft compensating open space per lot. Ordinance number not found.

component: Chapter 42 amendments extend the urban small-lot rules to the whole city with wastewater service
coverage: Citywide where wastewater collection service exists; outside Loop 610 phased: tracts of 1 acre or more from 2014-04-24, most tracts under 1 acre from 2015-04-24
coding_notes: City implementation memo (2013-05-03): amendments effective 2013-05-24; sections 42-181 to 42-185 (lot size, compensating open space, performance standards, lot width) phased outside Loop 610 as in coverage. Council vote 13-3 (Mercatus). Ordinance number (2013-343 in the policy inventory) not verified. Owners can still petition for special minimum lot size areas (70% of the area complying). Second coder (2026-10-18): effective date, phase-in and 3,500 sq ft minimum confirmed.

component: Livable Places amendments: second dwelling unit size cap raised from 900 to 1,500 sq ft
coverage: Citywide (development and redevelopment inside city limits); active deed restrictions still apply
coding_notes: by_right left null: Houston has no zoning, so no zoning approval is needed, but deed restrictions can forbid ADUs. Owner occupancy not mentioned.

component: Livable Places amendments: small multi-unit residential (3 to 8 units) and courtyard lots without street frontage
coverage: Citywide inside city limits; active deed restrictions still apply
coding_notes: Height limit applies (value not on the press release). Same caveat on deed restrictions as the ADU row.

component: Unified Development Code amendments: ADUs may have separate utilities, one-bedroom limit removed, up to two stories, smaller setbacks
parking: a parking space required for larger ADUs
coding_notes: Council approved 191 UDC amendments (article dated 2022-11-03, vote 'Thursday' = 2022-11-03); changes take effect Jan. 1 (2023). Owner occupancy already required by city ordinance and kept. ADU size cap, ADUs per lot and by-right status not in the source: left null. Second coder (2026-10-18) supplied the UDC text: owner occupancy confirmed (the owner must live in the principal unit or the ADU and may not rent the owner-occupied unit). Size: an ADU may not exceed 800 sq ft or 50% of the primary structure's gross floor area (excluding covered porches), up to 1,600 sq ft, in single-family districts other than FR; 1,200 sq ft in RE. adu_max_sqft=800 is the size every lot gets (same convention as Columbus: the floor of the cap). Source link for the UDC section still to add.

component: SB 15 (2025): new single-family tracts of 5+ acres with no recorded plat cannot be required to have lots over 3,000 sq ft (30 ft wide, 75 ft deep); small lots (<=4,000 sq ft) get caps on setbacks, parking, open space and stories
parking: small lots: no covered or off-site parking, at most 1 space per unit
coverage: Cities over 150,000 people wholly or partly in a county over 300,000; unplatted tracts of 5 acres or more zoned single-family; excludes land near airports and military bases
coding_notes: Signed 2025-06-20 (adoption_date = signature). Covers Austin, Houston, San Antonio, Dallas, Fort Worth and other large cities, but only new subdivisions of 5+ acres: little effect on infill. Setbacks capped at 15 ft front, 10 ft back, 5 ft side; open space/permeable cap 30%; must allow 3 stories. HOA and deed restrictions still apply. parking_min_per_unit is the cap on what a city may require.

component: SB 840 (2025): multifamily and mixed-use allowed by right in zones that allow office, commercial, retail or warehouse use; commercial-to-residential conversions
parking: at most 1 space per unit; no multilevel structure
coverage: Cities over 150,000 people wholly or partly in a county over 300,000; excludes heavy-industrial zones, land within 1,000 ft of heavy industry and 3,000 ft of airports or military bases
coding_notes: Density floor: the greater of the city's highest residential density or 36 units/acre; height floor 45 ft; setbacks at most 25 ft; no FAR limit; administrative approval. Coded theme=other (commercial land, not single-family lots): a confounder for 2025+ multifamily counts in large cities, not a missing-middle treatment.

component: HB 24 (2025): protest of a rezoning that allows more housing needs owners of 60% of adjoining land (was 20%) and is overridden by a simple majority (was three-fourths); comprehensive rezonings exempt from protest
coverage: All Texas municipalities with zoning; applies to proposals made on or after 2025-09-01
coding_notes: Old 20% threshold is the repealed Sec. 211.006(d) (from the policy inventory; the enrolled text keeps 20% for other changes). Process reform: changes the cost of upzoning, not the headroom of any lot.

component: SB 1883 (2025): impact fees need a two-thirds council vote, an independent audit before increases, and cannot rise again for 3 years; AG may sue
coverage: All political subdivisions charging Chapter 395 impact fees; applies to fees adopted or increased on or after 2025-09-01
coding_notes: Procedural: sets no fee amount, so fee_change_usd is null. May slow future increases (e.g. Austin Water impact fees).

component: HB 852 (2019): residential building permit and inspection fees cannot be based on the home's value or construction cost
coverage: All Texas municipalities; residential permit and inspection fees assessed on or after the effective date
coding_notes: Effective 2019-09-01 unless passed by two-thirds (immediate effect); the vote record was not checked. Valuation-based permit fees end, which also matters for permits' valuation_usd fields after 2019 (cities may stop collecting value).
